desk_read: Energy markets showed strong bullish appetite yesterday, led by WTI Crude Oil rallying +2.88% alongside a +6.1k contracts rise in total open interest that points directly to new longs, while the CLZ26-CLK27 spread held firm in backwardation at +9.34 $/bbl. Natural Gas also advanced +4.45% on volume at 1.1x its 20-day average, though its total open interest fell -7.3k contracts, signaling short covering on the move. Meanwhile, Gold ticked down -0.56% with total open interest dropping -815 contracts to mark long liquidation. In equities, S&P 500 gained +0.32% while total open interest fell -7.4k contracts, and Nasdaq 100 rose +0.56% with total open interest adding +672 contracts for new longs.
oil_read: Yesterday, WTI (CLZ26) rallied +2.88% with total open interest up +6.1k contracts (+0.5%) on 1.0x average volume, indicating new longs and backwardation with the CLZ26-CLK27 spread at +9.34 $/bbl. Meanwhile, Brent (BZF27) gained +2.04% alongside +876 contracts (+0.7%) of total open interest on 0.9x average volume, reflecting new longs and backwardation as the BZZ26-BZK27 spread settled at +14.12 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil and Brent (NYMEX) both print a bias mildly bullish through new longs, meaning fresh positioning supports the current upward move despite a weakening curve in backwardation. Nasdaq 100 also shows a bias mildly bullish via new longs, reinforcing the supportive trend structure in tech. Conversely, Silver displays a bias mildly bearish from new shorts, warning of a potential downward continuation. Natural Gas, Gold, Copper, and S&P 500 all sit at bias neutral due to position closures like short covering and long liquidation, indicating moves that lack durable participation. Overall, the short-term horizon reveals selective new capital in crude and tech while broader markets stall on liquidations.
